title: Inference Launch Contingency & Runbook Handoff
summary: Handoff of launch contingency runbook for upcoming inference feature set. We validated fallback paths, clarified ownership for degraded SLO scenarios, and captured action items to harden automations and runbook docs. Quick triage playbooks reviewed for KV cache pressure, kernel fallback, and cross-region failover.
topics: Automated fallback triggers (model variant, region, capacity tier)
KV cache eviction and prefix caching behavior
action_items: Priya: Update runbook Postmortem section with incident timeline template (due: 2026-11-24)
Samir: Add automated playbook steps to PagerDuty runbook for KV cache high-water alerts (due: 2026-11-22)
Marina: Validate model-variant compatibility matrix and add to runbook (due: 2026-11-23)
Lina: Run a regional failover dry-run on staging and capture latency SLO delta (due: 2026-11-25)
Alex: Add rollback checklist to release pipeline (feature flag, DB migrations if any) (due: 2026-11-22)
Zoe: Add token-level cost traces to the canary dashboard and set anomaly alert (due: 2026-11-24)
Diego: Create two regression test prompts that exercise long context + streaming edge cases (due: 2026-11-23)
Jonah: Coordinate on-call rotations and escalation for the 72h post-launch window (due: 2026-11-21)
next_steps: Share updated runbook doc link in #launch-readiness when PR is ready
Schedule canary surge rehearsal (Priya + Lina to pick window)
Run the KV cache chaos test on staging next Tuesday
Confirm SOC2 audit snapshot window won't overlap with canary
competitors_mentioned: Other cloud endpoints (generic) - noted as point of comparison for fallback speeds
Hyperscaler managed endpoints - in context of autoscaler limits
transcript_header:
Date: 2026-11-20 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Priya Desai (PM), Samir Patel (SRE), Marina Lopez (Runtime Eng), Owen Brooks (Product Ops), Diego Hu (QA), Lina Park (Infra), Alex Kim (Release Eng), Zoe Tran (Observability), Jonah Reed (Oncall)
Recording source: internal zoom
Notes: informal, some cross-talk; auto-transcript with minor mis-hearings
transcript:
[00:00] Priya (PM): Okay, starting on time — thanks everyone. This is the runbook handoff for the inference launch, I'm going to run through the contingency playbooks and then we will go round robin for ownership.
[00:14] Samir (SRE): Hey, quick note - the KV cache play looks like the highest risk for initial traffic spikes, we've seen that bite us last quarter.
[00:22] Marina (Runtime Eng): yeah, the K-V cash, sorry K-V cash, we've had a few mis-estimates on prefix cache hit rates — streaming sessions with long context just chew the cache.
[00:35] Priya: Right, so first play is KV cache pressure. Owner: Samir. Steps: detect high eviction rate, throttle low-priority requests, switch offending routes to smaller model-variant, and if that fails - region reroute. We have a draft automation for eviction alerts?
[00:52] Samir: There's a webhook today that flags eviction pct > 12% for three minutes but that's noisy. Need to add a rolling baseline and trigger only on sustained deviation. Also consider token-level cost tag correlation so we can know whether it's bursty user-induced or a systemic issue.
[01:10] Zoe (Obs): I can add cost traces, but need the canary dashboard metric name. Is it token.unitCost or token_cost? The transcript generator had it as token dot cost earlier — just checking.
[01:23] Marina: it's token_cost (we use underscore in the pipeline) but the exported logs sometimes show token.cost which confuses the dashboard. That's one of those parser mismatch things.
[01:36] Owen (Prod Ops): For the runbook wording — we should include exact Slack / PD messages to post. When we say 'notify product' we should tag the right channel and include a snippet. Otherwise people won't know what to do during the surge.
[01:50] Priya: Agreed. We'll add a templated PD trigger and a sample Slack post.
[01:55] Diego (QA): Are we doing a synthetic load that exercises the streaming + long-context combo? The edge case in question 7 failed in staging last night.
[02:07] Marina: Not that exact combo. Diego, can you write two prompts that reproduce the memory growth we saw? Put them in the regression suite and mark them as flaky-> must-pass for release.
[02:22] Diego: Yep.
[02:25] Jonah (Oncall): On escalation, who is first responder if it's model-quality degradation vs infra degradation? We need clear separation because the runbook has combined steps at the moment.
[02:36] Priya: Good call. We'll separate into SRE-first for infra signals (latency, OOMs, KV eviction) and Runtime/ML for hallucination or output-quality signals. Jonah, add the first responder at the top-level of the playbook.
[02:47] Jonah: Will do.
[02:49] [03:01] Lina (Infra): I want to call out region failover. The play currently says 'shift traffic to region B' but we need to validate kernel compatibility for quantized weights prior to shifting — otherwise we get inference errors. Marina, do we have a compatibility matrix?
[03:18] Marina: We have a draft, but it doesn't cover the latest quant kernels. I'll validate and add to runbook.
[03:26] Alex (Release Eng): For rollback - checklist must include feature-flag toggles, consumer-facing API contract checks, and confirm DB schema didn't change. We should keep rollback < 15 minutes for this launch.
[03:40] Priya: 15 min rollback target noted. Alex, add steps and timing estimates.
[03:45] Alex: On it.
[03:48] [04:02] Zoe: Observability - I recommend adding a token-level latency distribution and a cost-per-token anomaly alert. If cost-per-token spikes with low latency, that's likely an encoder/decoder regression.
[04:16] Samir: Also tie in the KV-hit ratio to the canary so we don't confuse warmup effects. If canary is cold, hit ratio will be low for first 10 mins.
[04:28] Priya: We'll add a warmup guard and a canary grace period.
[04:31] [05:00] Marina: There's also the kernel fallback path: if custom kernel fails, fall back to generic kernel with slightly higher latency but preserves correctness. Need to set the metric to fail at 1% error rate for 2 consecutive minutes.
[05:14] Lina: Generic kernels increase GPU memory usage, beware of OOM ripple. We should trigger autoscale before fallback if possible.
[05:26] Priya: So the order is autoscale -> model variant downgrade -> kernel fallback -> region reroute -> degrade gracefully (partial response?) -> rollback. Does that match everyone's mental model?
[05:40] Marina: Yes.
[05:43] [06:00] Diego: QA note — partial response mode must include a specific client error code so SDKs can surface it. Please add that to API contract checklist.
[06:12] Alex: We'll add an HTTP 429 with structured explain field, or maybe 503 with retry-after; need to align with SDK folks.
[06:22] Priya: Add 429 for rate-limited degrade and 503 for full outage. Diego, add to API test matrix.
[06:31] [07:00] Owen: Legal/Security check — does canary include any PII folks? We need to filter prompt logs and ensure KMS wrapping during the canary.
[07:12] Priya: KMS reviews are done for this launch, but we will include a canary scrubber step to avoid raw PII in logs. Lina, ensure KMS key rotation doesn't conflict with staging keys.
[07:24] Lina: noted.
[07:27] [08:00] Priya: Let's go around quickly for final ownership confirmation. Samir?
[08:04] Samir: I'll own KV cache play, add automation tuning.
[08:08] Marina: Runtime will own kernel fallback and model-variant mapping.
[08:11] Alex: Rollback checklist and release pipeline gating - I'll own.
[08:15] Zoe: Observability metrics and dashboarding - I'll own.
[08:18] Diego: QA will add regression prompts and API contract tests.
[08:22] Jonah: Oncall escalation and rotation sheet - I'll own.
[08:25] Priya: Great. A couple of detailed points then we'll capture action items.
[08:31] [08:45] Priya: Regarding the SLO thresholds - we set the immediate alert at p95 latency > 750ms sustained for 3 minutes AND token_cost spike > 2x baseline. That's the combinatoric rule to reduce false positives. Thoughts?
[09:00] Samir: Sounds OK. I suggest adding a fallback rule that if error-rate climbs > 0.5% within 2 minutes we trigger canary rollback immediately.
[09:12] Marina: Agree on error-rate trigger.
[09:14] [09:30] Owen: For post-incident comms, do we have a template for customer-facing status page messaging versus internal postmortem? We need both.
[09:45] Priya: We'll include both templates. Internal postmortem must include timelines, root cause hypotheses, actions, and RCA owner. Customer-facing must be high level and empathetic.
[09:58] [10:15] Diego: Quick transcription note — auto transcript sometimes swaps 'quant' with 'count' — expect some mis-words in minutes.
[10:23] Priya: Good note, we'll proof the runbook language.
[10:26] [11:00] Priya: Any blockers that will prevent us from delivering the runbook updates by end of week? If no, then we should commit.
[11:08] Marina: Only blocker is kernel compatibility matrix completion, two-day work. Not blocking the doc though.
[11:15] Lina: Region failover dry-run scheduling might conflict with another team on Thursday, but we can rebook.
[11:22] Priya: Ok, we'll escalate scheduling conflicts if any.
[11:28] [12:00] Priya: Alright, recap: owners and due dates captured, Samir will tune alerts, Alex will add rollback checklist, Diego will add QA prompts, Zoe will add cost traces, Marina will finish compatibility matrix, Lina will schedule regional dry-run, Jonah will own rotations. We'll publish updated runbook PR and ping #launch-readiness. Any final comments?
[12:18] Samir: Just one more — please include a small table in the runbook of quick mitigation snippets (commands, service names). It saves minutes in incident.
[12:27] Priya: Absolutely. We'll include command snippets.
[12:31] [12:45] Priya: Thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.
[12:52] END: Meeting ended at 17:02 UTC.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions (quant->count, KV cache->K-V cash), speaker overlaps at 02:20 and 08:00, timestamps are approximate.
